complexityManagement.behavior: The account view stays architectural; stages and stacks are the only deployment-boundary containers on the overview.
Views offer deployable service resources. Resource internals such as routes, policy statements, indexes, event targets, and Lambda permissions appear only after opening their owner.
API, Lambda, messaging, data, security, identity, networking, observability, and workflow views keep one vocabulary per problem while preserving shared resources as endpoints.
Scalar AWS properties, CloudFormation expressions, policies, OpenAPI fragments, ASL JSON, tags, imports, and lifecycle controls remain in the attributes/details pane instead of becoming graph nodes.
Only deploy, dependency, invocation, event/message flow, data access, authorization, role use, encryption, observation, and workflow transition references become edges.

Common multi-object AWS integrations render as clean edges backed by relationship-view objects; the intermediate policy, subscription, mapping, and notification objects remain editable in their owners.
Far zoom emphasizes containers and resource identity; normal zoom shows resource cards; near zoom reveals selected details and edge labels.
Traceability and production-readiness objects are separate overlays so governance information does not compete with runtime topology.
